entries.summary: November 14 17:09 EST: Bearish — Elevated Downside Risk unchanged for November 16–18; Moderate confidence and Very High event risk. Saturday non-trading interval: latest US cash closes remain Friday Nasdaq -0.91%, QQQ about -1.19%, SOX -3.4%, versus SOX +8.1% weekly. Open Watch has 163 curated events (last update 2026-11-13T23:46:19+00:00), unchanged. Asynchronous reported 10Y 5.133% and 2Y 4.850% imply +28.3bp, not a synchronized close. Brent Friday settlement $95.84/bbl; WTI $88.57/bbl is an asynchronous quote. November 14 reporting adds no independently verified material new US market catalyst. November 16 Empire State survey, November 17 retail sales and Nvidia earnings after close, November 18 FOMC minutes remain pivotal. Synchronized VIX/VXN, full Nasdaq breadth and direct CME FedWatch are unavailable.
bullish: Nasdaq gained 2.3% for the week despite Friday's -0.91% decline (AP), showing residual demand.
October PPI +0.3% month-on-month versus +0.4% expected offers limited inflation relief.
An oversold rebound could develop if SOX relative strength, breadth and volatility confirm it.

MarketWatch/Barron's report SOX gained approximately 8.1% across the week despite Friday's -3.4% fall; Friday equal-weight S&P 500 RSP rose 0.19% in secondary reporting, suggesting rotation rather than indiscriminate selling.
Barron's November 14 review confirms the semiconductor index rose over 8% during the week, suggesting Friday's decline did not erase prior sector recovery.

Reuters November 9 brokerage survey reports several banks considered AI-sector selling overdone and highlighted longer-term infrastructure spending; these are analyst opinions, not confirmed Friday reversal.

TechCrunch November 14 reports South Korea's Science Ministry says Nvidia reaffirmed plans to supply 260,000 advanced GPUs and continue joint AI projects; prospective supply continuity, not a new US trading reaction.
bearish: Friday Nasdaq -0.91% versus Dow +0.09% shows technology-specific pressure; Nvidia closed -2.01% at $162.85.
WSJ reports SOX closed -3.4% Friday, with AMD -8.8% and Broadcom -4.8% per AP, confirming semiconductor-specific weakness.
Friday WSJ 10Y 5.133% and 2Y 4.850% indicate elevated yields and a +28.3bp curve spread at reported quotes; not matched closing data.
Nvidia earnings expected Tuesday after close create significant Wednesday repricing risk.

Friday QQQ -1.19% versus equal-weight RSP +0.19% and semiconductor ETF SMH -3.05% in secondary post-close reporting confirm technology concentration, though ETF quotes are not synchronized primary exchange prints.
Saturday Times reporting estimates Nvidia -12.8% for the week and $573bn of five-day market-cap erosion, reinforcing AI leadership shock; secondary figures, not a fresh Saturday market move.
Barron's November 14 preview identifies anticipated Anthropic IPO pricing Wednesday as another possible AI sentiment test; expected timing and impact remain unverified.
StoneX November 14 weekend USD/JPY outlook describes sharp hawkish Fed repricing and elevated Treasury yields, a cross-asset valuation headwind; no synchronized new Treasury quotes are inferred.
November 13 Motley Fool closing coverage attributes further Nvidia pressure to an HSBC downgrade to Hold; already reflected in Friday's -2.01% close, not a fresh post-close decline.
TechCrunch November 14 describes continued Asian policy uncertainty over restricted Nvidia chips and Chinese projects; no enacted new US export restriction established.

editorial.marketOverview: US equity markets were closed Saturday, so Friday's Nasdaq -0.91%, QQQ about -1.19% and SOX -3.4% remain the last relevant cash-session moves. Semiconductors underperformed on Friday despite an approximately 8.1% weekly advance, creating a fragile but not one-sided technical backdrop. High reported yields continue to challenge growth-stock valuations, but available bond quotes are not synchronized.
editorial.whatChanged: Relative to the November 14 16:18 EST snapshot, no verified material directional catalyst or new curated Open Watch event appeared. The 163-event Open Watch file is unchanged, with its latest timestamp 2026-11-13T23:46:19+00:00. Weekend calendar cross-checks confirm previously anticipated November 16–18 releases and earnings; previews are not realized market reactions.
editorial.marketInterpretation: Technology and chip concentration remain the strongest downside signals. Friday's equal-weight S&P proxy resilience and SOX's weekly gain suggest rotation and residual demand rather than a verified broad-market liquidation. The reported 5.133% 10Y and 4.850% 2Y imply +28.3 basis points, not 283 or 2.83; because observation times are not matched, the spread is indicative only. A secondary 91% December hike probability must not be mistaken for a live CME FedWatch reading.
editorial.threeDayPath: Monday November 16 could see fragile positioning ahead of Empire State manufacturing data and Tuesday's high-impact events. Tuesday November 17 retail sales can alter rates and Nasdaq duration sensitivity before Nvidia's after-close earnings. Wednesday November 18 may be dominated by the first cash-session reaction to Nvidia's report and later FOMC minutes. These are conditional scenarios, not predictions of released results or guaranteed market direction.
editorial.bullCase: A better-than-feared macro release, falling synchronized Treasury yields and renewed SOX leadership with improving Nasdaq breadth could turn Friday's semiconductor weakness into a temporary shakeout. Nvidia results and guidance could restore confidence if market reaction, rather than the headline alone, confirms buying.
editorial.bearCase: Persistent high yields, renewed Nvidia governance or export-control pressure, poor retail-sales interpretation, and negative SOX/QQQ price confirmation could extend downside. Nvidia's earnings and Wednesday's minutes make event risk unusually high; secondary implied-move estimates indicate uncertainty, not direction.
editorial.watchNext: Track Monday's Empire State release and opening breadth; verify matched VXN/VIX and Treasury 2Y/10Y timestamps if available. On Tuesday compare retail sales to consensus and observe actual rates/QQQ response; after Nvidia earnings, distinguish guidance from Wednesday's sector-wide reaction. Monitor FOMC minutes and any newly curated Open Watch event. A sustained QQQ recovery supported by SOX, breadth and easing yields would challenge bearish bias; renewed SOX lows with widening volatility would reinforce it.
